assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defines incretin physiology and converted it into GLP-1-based drugs that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care. A rare combination of a clear physiological discovery, a mechanistic bridge to therapy and very large patient benefit.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 physiology and secretion in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, intestinotrophic and metabolic actions) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide) form a defensible trio. Knudsen's medicinal-chemistry role in liraglutide/semaglutide development and the contributions of others to the original GLP-1 work are not fully resolved by the supplied credit; I have not independently verified priority claims.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drugs, and outcome trials showing cardiovascular and renal benefits. Timely and arguably at full maturity.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on physiology or on drug development, which changes the laureate set.
Priority disputes over who first identified the active GLP-1 peptide are not settled by the supplied evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically targeted, millisecond-precise optical control of defined cell types, enabling causal dissection of neural circuits and now early clinical use in vision restoration. Methodologically transformative across neuroscience and physiology.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and the neuronal implementation (Boyden, Deisseroth, with Miesenboeck's earlier related approach) are separable contributions; only three can be named. My selection favours the discovery of the light-gated channel plus the most prominent neuronal application, and I acknowledge that Boyden and Bamberg have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of widespread, independent adoption and a stable interpretation. Recognition is mature and arguably overdue as a tool-based discovery.
uncertainties: Allocation among six credited names is a real obstacle; any trio leaves out a strong claimant.
Direct therapeutic impact is still limited, so the case rests on the research-tool value.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-driven antisense correction of SMN2 exon 7 splicing produced nusinersen, the first effective therapy for a fatal childhood neurodegenerative disease. The path from splicing mechanism to approved drug is unusually clear and clinically dramatic.
assessment.attribution: Krainer provided the splicing-regulation mechanism and target identification and Bennett the antisense chemistry and drug development; the two-person configuration is clean in the supplied credit. Contributions from others (for example the SMN1/SMN2 genetics and the Ionis/Biogen clinical teams) are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016, with long-term follow-up data and stronger therapeutic validity than many alternatives. Timing is reasonable though the field is younger than the leading candidates.
uncertainties: Antisense oligonucleotide chemistry builds on earlier work whose credit might be considered.
Long-term durability and the relative importance versus gene therapy are still being evaluated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, establishing a new cancer-treatment modality with clear conceptual originality.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T translation, costimulatory design) and Sadelain (CD28 costimulation in CARs, preclinical proof) are strong; Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy contributions and early CAR concepts, notably from Eshhar who is not in the credited list, complicate the story.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and more than a decade of clinical data, with emerging use in autoimmunity. Maturity is good although long-term safety, secondary malignancies and solid-tumour limits remain.
uncertainties: Eshhar's foundational chimeric receptor concept is not among the credited names, which weakens a fair allocation.
Overlap with Rosenberg's adoptive transfer work makes the boundary of the discovery unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level reductions in disease demonstrated. A strong example of preventive vaccinology rooted in a clear mechanistic insight about L1 self-assembly.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (NCI, L1 VLP immunogenicity) and Frazer (VLP expression and vaccine development in Australia) are the central names; Jian Zhou, who contributed to the VLP work, is not in the credited list and the allocation among groups is somewhat contested.
assessment.maturity: Real-world effectiveness data from national programmes are now available. Timing is appropriate, and the link to cervical cancer reduction strengthens the case.
uncertainties: Priority among groups developing L1 VLPs is disputed and was not independently verified.
Recognition of zur Hausen's earlier prize may make the committee view this as partly covered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery that the endoplasmic reticulum signals to the nucleus to adjust folding capacity, a fundamental cell-biological principle with implications for neurodegeneration, diabetes and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and complementarily defined the Ire1-Hac1/XBP1 pathway; the two-name credit is clean. Contributions of Kozutsumi and others to early identification are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Pathway well established for decades and broadly confirmed in many species. Therapeutic translation is still partial, but the basic principle is solid.
uncertainties: Clinical impact is more indirect than for the higher-ranked candidates.
Whether Walter's work on the integrated stress response and other co-workers should be recognised is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational targeting of BCR-ABL with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one and served as the prototype for oncogene-targeted therapy.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development), Lydon (compound discovery) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) are credited; the underlying BCR-ABL fusion discovery by Rowley, Nowell and others and Wittes/Zimmermann (Novartis chemistry) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of outcomes data and widely validated. Perhaps somewhat late in the sense that its prototype role is long past, with Lasker recognition already given.
uncertainties: Earlier Nobel-recognised work on oncogenes and the contribution of Novartis chemists complicate attribution.
Whether the committee views it as a drug-development prize rather than a discovery is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishment of long-term self-renewing three-dimensional organoids from single adult Lgr5-positive stem cells, enabling human disease modelling, drug testing and personalised medicine research.
assessment.attribution: Clevers (Lgr5 stem cell identification and organoid concept) and Sato (the culture system, first author of the key papers) form a clean pair. Contributions from the earlier embryonic and pluripotent organoid field, such as Sasai, are not included.
assessment.maturity: Technique widely adopted with strong independent confirmation, but clinical impact is still emerging and the advance is largely a method for research.
uncertainties: Clinical benefit is not yet established beyond research applications.
Overlap with pluripotent-stem-cell-derived organoid work may complicate the scope of the discovery.
